sentences: A fat graph minor models vertices and edges by connected pieces that remain separated except at prescribed incidences.
The source asks whether excluding a fixed such pattern forces balanced separators coverable by roughly a square-root number of bounded-radius balls.
A related version assumes exclusion of an induced minor.
The separator may contain many vertices, so its economical description is metric coverage rather than cardinality alone.
The conjecture seeks a usable separator theorem from coarse geometric restrictions that are weaker than ordinary excluded-minor structure.
